assessment_summary:
Step 1. Let T be a tree on n vertices with 2 <= n <= 7. (Justified: Proof setup.)
Step 2. Let l be the number of leaves in T. (Justified: Variable assignment.)
Step 3. By definition, a leaf is a vertex of degree 1 in T. (Justified: Uses the given definition.)
Step 4. Let v be a vertex in T such that its degree is Delta(T). (Justified: Every finite graph has a vertex of maximum degree.)
Step 5. If we remove vertex v and its incident edges from T, the remaining graph consists of exactly Delta(T) connected components. (Justified: Removing a vertex of degree k from a tree leaves k components.)
Step 6. Let these components be C_1, C_2, ..., C_{Delta(T)}. (Justified: Naming the components.)
Step 7. Because T is a tree, it contains no cycles, meaning each component C_i is also a tree. (Justified: Subgraphs of trees are acyclic, and components are connected.)
Step 8. Every tree has at least two leaves. (Objection: False. A tree on 1 vertex (K1) has degree 0, so it has 0 leaves by the degree 1 definition.)
Step 9. Therefore, each component C_i contains at least two vertices of degree 1 within C_i. (Objection: Follows from the flawed Step 8.)
Step 10. For each component C_i, exactly one vertex was adjacent to v in the original tree T. (Justified: If more than one vertex were adjacent to v, T would contain a cycle.)
Step 11. The degree of this connection vertex is 1 higher in T than it is in C_i. (Justified: The connection vertex gains the edge to v.)
Step 12. The degrees of all other vertices in C_i remain unchanged when transitioning back to T. (Justified: No other edges involving C_i are present in T.)
Step 13. Since C_i has at least two leaves (degree 1) and only one vertex changes degree, at least one leaf in C_i remains a leaf in T. (Justified: Follows logically from the preceding steps.)
Step 14. This implies that each of the Delta(T) components contributes at least one distinct leaf to T. (Justified: Each component contributes its distinct leaf.)
Step 15. Thus, T has at least Delta(T) leaves, giving l >= Delta(T). (Justified: Summing over the Delta(T) components.)
Step 16. In any tree with n <= 7, there are always at least two vertices that are not leaves and are not the maximum degree vertex. (Objection: False. A star graph K_{1, n-1} contains only the central vertex and leaves, leaving no other vertices.)
Step 17. These two extra internal vertices must each branch out, creating at least one additional leaf each. (Objection: Follows from the flawed Step 16.)
Step 18. Therefore, the total number of leaves must be at least Delta(T) + 2. (Objection: Follows from the flawed Step 17.)
counterexample: The star graph K_{1,3} on 4 vertices has maximum degree Delta(T) = 3 and 3 leaves. The statement asserts it has at least 3 + 2 = 5 leaves, which is false.
